impact:
A food with zero protein or zero calories cannot be logged. The user works around it by entering 0.1.

WHERE THE DEFECT IS
- apps/web/src/screens/start/FuelPanel.tsx:76 — canAddCustom requires isPositive(customProtein) AND isPositive(customCalories).
- apps/web/src/screens/start/FuelPanel.tsx:27 — isPositive is strictly > 0.
- The Add button is disabled on that flag (FuelPanel.tsx:204).

WHERE THE SYMPTOM IS TRIGGERED FROM
FuelPanel is rendered on the Start screen (apps/web/src/screens/start/StartScreen.tsx) — the "Log something else" form, FuelPanel.tsx:173-207.

THE API ALREADY ACCEPTS ZERO
apps/api/src/routes/fuel.ts:87-100 clamps with Math.max(0, ...) and requires only a non-empty label. The column defaults are 0 and NOT NULL (apps/api/src/db/schema/tracker.ts:166-167). So this is purely a frontend gate against values the backend was designed to store.

WHAT IT COSTS
- Zero-protein foods are most of what people eat: olive oil, rice, fruit, bread, soda, beer. None can be logged honestly.
- Zero-calorie items — black coffee, diet soda, sugar-free gum, greens — cannot be logged at all.
- The 0.1 workaround corrupts the data it was invented to save: 0.1 g entries accumulate into the protein total (fuel.ts:75-78) and into the history chart (fuel.ts:126-160), so adherence is scored against numbers the user knows are fiction.

FIX
Replace the both-must-be-positive gate with: label non-empty AND at least one of protein/calories is a finite number >= 0, with both fields actually filled (empty string is a different state from 0 and should read as "not entered"). Keep rejecting negatives and NaN. A single-field entry — 120 kcal, no protein — is the common case and must be one tap away.

Note: FuelPanel.tsx:87 uses the same isPositive gate for the nutrition TARGET form. A zero target is a different question (a target of 0 kcal is probably a mistake) — decide it deliberately rather than changing it as a side effect of this fix.
resolution:
Fixed by modelling a fuel amount as three states instead of a number.

New apps/web/src/lib/fuel.ts holds the rule as pure functions, with apps/web/src/lib/fuel.test.ts beside it (the lib/api/errors.ts pattern):
- Amount is { blank } | { entered, value } | { invalid }. Blank is deliberately not zero: "I have not said" and "it is none" were the same value under the old numberOf(), and telling them apart is the whole fix.
- canLogAmounts(protein, calories) — a food must declare at LEAST ONE of its two numbers, neither may be unreadable or negative. Olive oil (0 g protein) and black coffee (0 kcal) now log honestly; both-blank is still refused.
- isUsableTarget() keeps the old both-must-be-positive rule for the nutrition TARGET form, which is a separate question: a target of 0 kcal is a mistake, not a fact. Deliberately unchanged rather than swept along.
- amountValue() / bumpAmount() replace numberOf() / bump(); a blank field contributes 0 to a total and steps up from 0.

FuelPanel.tsx now reads the gate from that module: canAddCustom at :69-70, canSaveTarget at :81, and NumberField's steppers at :259/:271. The local numberOf/bump/isPositive helpers and the NumberDraft alias are gone.

The API needed no change — fuel.ts:87-100 already clamped with Math.max(0, ...) and the columns already default to 0.

VERIFIED: pnpm --filter @afya/web typecheck (clean), test (34 passed, 4 files), lint (clean). 14 new assertions cover the zero cases that were impossible before. NOT verified at runtime against a live API.
title: Fuel will not log a food with zero protein or zero calories, forcing a 0.1 workaround that corrupts the totals
